item.title: Unauthorized / Incorrect Road Closure, 20th September
item.description:
Unauthorized / Incorrect Road Closure (9:00 AM): This morning, Evesham Road Hyde Lane and Southam Lane Junction was entirely closed off with a diversion sign placed directly at the traffic lights. Because of this incorrect closure, I was forced to turn into oncoming traffic at 9:00 AM just to safely access my place of work, creating a severe and unacceptable safety hazard. Conflicting & Negligent Signage: The signage displayed at the intersection was entirely contradictory. Signs stated both "Road ahead closed access only", "Cheltenham half marathon green car park ONLY" and "DIVERSION". At no point did any signage indicate that local businesses on Evesham Road were open as usual, turning away crucial Sunday trading footfall. Public Interference & Self-Correction (10:30 AM): Due to the lack of clear management or marshal presence at this position, a member of the public moved the diversion sign at 10:30 AM to allow access. To protect oncoming drivers and ensure cars could turn into the road safely, I had to personally lay the misleading diversion sign flat and relocate the remaining signs. I have attached a picture I took before moving the signs. Please note that whilst I was approaching the junction, there was nearly a collision where a driver had braked suddenly, seemingly confused over the directions. The placement of these signs represents a severe lack of oversight by the event organisers and the Council's highway licensing team. It actively choked off trade for an open business while forcing drivers into dangerous manoeuvres.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Evesham Road, Bishop's Cleeve, Tewkesbury

item.title: Traffic Lights on Cheltenham Road by Greyhound Pub, 20th September
item.description:
Coming from Cheltenham down golden valley to Longlevens is horrendous every day from 3.15pm onwards. The queues are related to one small thing - traffic lights. The issue is those who want to turn right into Greyhound Gardens are unable too, due to the amount of oncoming traffic. This is then causing the traffic as no one behind them can continue straight. The simplest solution is 1) make a right filter only so the oncoming traffic stops. You have this filter on Innsworth Lane by Nick Brown butchers to go into Longford Lane. 2) Do what you have done with Innsworth Lane / Parton Road in Churchdown by Hare Hounds Pub. Innsworth Lane goes and Parton Road opposite are on red. Then Parton Road goes and Innsworth Lane Red. This has reduced congestion on Parton Road as people can turn right onto Cheltenham Road East. This Greyhound Gardens issue is no different so why can't you do one of the above? It would make many drivers and me so happy. Thanks

item.title: 'No Entry' sign facing the wrong way. It is the right-hand of a group of three similar signs telling drivers not to enter the upper part of Montpellier Street, Cheltenham but is actually facing the Queens Hotel (ie, eastwards), suggesting no entry to Fauconberg Road. This is likely to confuse drivers who do not know the area. It should be facing the same way as the other two 'No Entry' signs, ie roughly southwards. It may have been twisted on the post by vandals., 19th September

item.title: Pigeon problem Under the bridge, 19th September
item.description:
The netting under the Honeybourne bridge on market street was removed because it was falling down one end and birds where getting trapped, it was also filling with rubbish, it looked much better. However the pigeons are now nesting and perching on the ledges under the bridge and causing a right mess. There is a thick layer of poo on the path and down the bridge walls, there are feathers starting to block the drain. We can’t park under the bridge as cars are covered with poo, walking under the bridge it is also risky trying not to get pooped on. It all looks very messy and is not very hygienic. It may need spikes attaching to the ledges to deter the birds. Thank you in advance.
